prf:tmli-constituent-composite-agreement:
Proof Proof that constituent and composite traces agree. Under the hypothesis, \beta_{\mathfrak{H}} is (up to cyclic rotation) a product w_0 w_1 \cdots w_{N-2} with w_i a word in \sigma_i^{\pm 1}, and the letters grouped at generator \sigma_i are exactly w_i, with Hecke reduction \rho(w_i) = a_i\sigma_i + b_i. The Markov trace product then gives \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})) = \prod_i (z\,a_i + b_i) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}}, and cyclicity of \mathrm{tr}_M covers the rotations.

For the counterexample, \sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0\sigma_1 = h\,\sigma_0\sigma_1\sigma_0 + \sigma_1\sigma_0 by the braid and Hecke relations, so its trace is h(hz^2 + z) + z^2, while the grouped product is (hz + 1)^2; these differ by z^2 - hz - 1 = -(q^4+q^2+1)/(q^2+1)^2. \square
prop:hecke-markov-transition:
Proposition Hecke generator as stochastic transition operator. The Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) and the Jones-Markov trace admit a direct probabilistic interpretation: each Hecke generator acts as a stochastic transition operator. The product factorization corresponds to independent one-step expectations along a Markov chain.

Let H_n(R, q) be the Iwahori-Hecke algebra.

(i) Spectral idempotents. The orthogonal idempotents

  e_+^{(i)} = \frac{\sigma_i + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}, \qquad
  e_-^{(i)} = \frac{q - \sigma_i}{q + q^{-1}}

satisfy e_+^{(i)} + e_-^{(i)} = 1, (e_\pm^{(i)})^2 = e_\pm^{(i)}, and e_+^{(i)} e_-^{(i)} = 0. They reconstruct the generator as \sigma_i = q \cdot e_+^{(i)} - q^{-1} \cdot e_-^{(i)}.

(ii) Transition probabilities. The symmetric and antisymmetric transition probabilities are p_+ = q^2/(q^2 + 1) and p_- = 1/(q^2 + 1). The stochastic transition operator at generator i is K_i = p_+ \cdot \mathrm{id} + p_- \cdot s_i, a row-stochastic matrix. The system stays in its configuration with probability p_+ or transposes with probability p_-.

(iii) Markov property as memorylessness. The Markov trace property requires the transition at generator n to depend only on the eigenvalue structure of \sigma_n, not on the history in H_{n-1}(q). The expectation value of the i-th crossing is \mathbb{E}[\hat{V}_i] = z \cdot a_i + b_i = \hat{V}_i, recovering the vertex volume.

(iv) Independence and factorization. The product formula factors as independent one-step expectations only when each generator occurs at most once in the word. Then the Markov property peels one generator at a time and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_{i_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_\ell}) = z^{\ell}. When a generator repeats the factorisation fails: for w = \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1, \mathrm{tr}_M(w) = h z^2 + z with h = q - q^{-1}, not z^3. So in general a vertex volume is not determined locally; it depends on the other generators in the word.

prf:hecke-markov-transition:
Proof Proof of hecke markov transition. (i) Direct computation from (\sigma_i - q)(\sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0. Since \sigma_i satisfies a quadratic with distinct roots q and -q^{-1}, the spectral projectors are e_\pm = (\sigma_i - \lambda_\mp)/(\lambda_\pm - \lambda_\mp). Substituting \lambda_+ = q, \lambda_- = -q^{-1} gives the stated formulas.

(ii) The element e_+^{(i)} = (\sigma_i + q^{-1})/(q + q^{-1}) acts on the q-eigenspace as the identity and on the (-q^{-1})-eigenspace as zero. In the permutation representation, the q-eigenspace is the in-order subspace (adjacent elements not transposed) and the (-q^{-1})-eigenspace is the transposed subspace. The convex combination K_i = p_+ \cdot \mathrm{id} + p_- \cdot s_i is manifestly stochastic (non-negative entries, rows summing to 1).

Since s_i acts by a permutation matrix, K_i is symmetric, so its columns also sum to 1: K_i is doubly stochastic, and its stationary law is the uniform measure on S_n, not the Mallows measure \pi(\sigma) \propto q^{\mathrm{inv}(\sigma)}. The Diaconis--Ram systematic-scan Metropolis chain [diaconis-ram2000], which does target the Mallows measure, accepts the transposition with a probability that depends on whether it creates an inversion; it is a different operator from K_i.

(iii) The Markov property \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(x) says that the contribution of the rightmost generator \sigma_n separates as the scalar factor z, regardless of the element x \in H_{n-1}(q). This is the memorylessness of a Markov chain: the transition at step n depends only on the crossing type at \sigma_n, not on the history of previous crossings.

(iv) Induction on \ell when each generator occurs at most once. Let \sigma_m be the letter of highest index, so the word is u\,\sigma_m\,v with u, v words in \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_{m-1}. By cyclicity of the trace, \mathrm{tr}_M(u\,\sigma_m\,v) = \mathrm{tr}_M(v u\,\sigma_m), and vu \in H_{m}(q) does not involve \sigma_m, so the Markov property gives \mathrm{tr}_M(vu\,\sigma_m) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(vu). The word vu has \ell - 1 letters, each generator still at most once, so by induction \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_{i_1}\cdots\sigma_{i_\ell}) = z^{\ell}, the base case being \mathrm{tr}_M(1) = 1. If a generator repeats, the remaining word is no longer in H_{m-1}(q) and the Markov property does not apply; the step fails (for \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1 one gets h z^2 + z \neq z^3). \square

Limiting behaviour

At q = 1 (classical limit), p_+ = p_- = 1/2 and the chain is a fair random walk on S_n. As q \to \infty (deep-quantum limit), p_+ \to 1 and the chain becomes deterministic: only the symmetric channel survives, recovering the totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP). For the aether value q = q_0, the per-step Shannon entropy H = -p_+\ln p_+ - p_-\ln p_- is close to the maximum \ln 2; the canonical evaluation is given in Chapter 7 (physical observations).
rem:hecke-markov-interpretation:
Remark Markov chain validation of the algebraic framework. Every algebraic construction possesses a Markov chain counterpart. The Hecke algebra H_n(R, q) is simultaneously a space of braid-group representations and stochastic transition operators.

SYT paths on the Young graph

Fix an irrep \lambda \vdash n. The Hoefsmit seminormal form builds \rho_\lambda on standard Young tableaux of shape \lambda. Each tableau is a saturated chain on the Young graph. The space of all valid SYTs serves as the discrete state space of the chain.

The generator \sigma_i \in B_n acts via \rho_\lambda(\sigma_i), whose non-zero matrix entries are explicit rational functions of q. This is a genuine quantum deformation of the classical Young seminormal form. The matrix entries are probability amplitudes. The entries can be negative and square to weights only after a Markov trace.

Two compatible pictures coexist:

  1. Amplitude picture. Amplitudes evolve a complex state vector on the SYT path space. The Jones polynomial is the closed-path sum over all SYT paths, matching the structure of a Feynman path integral.
  2. Probability picture. Summing amplitudes through spectral idempotents yields the classical stochastic operator K_i, which targets the Mallows measure.

The quadratic Hecke relation bridges these pictures. The amplitudes living on SYT edges square to the Boltzmann weights of the classical chain.

Jucys-Murphy cell reindexing

The Jucys-Murphy elements L_k act diagonally with eigenvalue q^{2 c_T(k)}. Because [L_i, L_j] = 0, all SYT cells couple uniformly. This uniformity constitutes the representation-theoretic origin of the all-pairs coupling observed in the mass-tower. The transition from amplitudes to probabilities mirrors the shift from generator indexing to cell indexing.

Non-local correlations

The memorylessness condition coexists with non-trivial correlations. Each step depends only on the current state. Yet the braid relations impose strict correlations between non-adjacent generators through the Yang-Baxter equation. Each crossing is a local transition determined solely by the eigenvalue structure. The non-local correlations are purely representation-theoretic constraints.

Planck steps

Each Markov step evaluates one Hecke crossing into its symmetric or antisymmetric channel. In the Reeb flow, this is one iteration on the exceptional divisor—a single Planck step. The q-deformation away from the fair coin strictly bounds the Shannon entropy below \ln 2, reducing the information content per crossing.

Continuous-time limit

In the continuous limit, the Markov chain becomes the asymmetric simple exclusion process (ASEP). The ASEP generator sums the Hecke algebra elements. The stationary distribution is the Mallows measure, which weights each permutation by q raised to its inversion number.

Physical observables represent expectations under this measure, computed via the Markov trace.

prop:q-gaussian-obstruction-at-q0:
Proposition Bożejko–Speicher q-Gaussian obstruction at the aether q_0 > 1. At the aether parameter q_0 \approx 1.10998 > 1, the Bożejko-Speicher non-commutative q-Gaussian (the q-Fock-space construction) does not exist. The sequence of even moments

  T_n(q_0) = \sum_{\pi} q_0^{\,\mathrm{cr}(\pi)}

(sum over perfect matchings \pi of [2n]) diverges super-exponentially. It is nevertheless a positive-definite moment sequence: its Jacobi coefficients are [k]_{q_0} = 1 + q_0 + \cdots + q_0^{k-1} > 0, so its Hankel determinants \prod_{k=1}^{n-1} [k]_{q_0}^{\,n-k} are positive and probability measures with these moments exist. None of them arises from the q-Fock construction, and none has a finite moment-generating function.

Braid-word fluctuations at q_0 cannot be modeled by the Bożejko-Speicher q-Gaussian. The valid substitutes are the inner Perron-Frobenius dominant eigenvalue and the outer Féray-Méliot q-Plancherel CLT.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It applies q-deformation identities over an abstract coefficient ring and specializes them to real-valued observables at q_0.
prf:q-gaussian-obstruction-at-q0:
Proof Proof of q gaussian obstruction at q0. Step 1 — maximal crossings. A perfect matching of [2n] has at most \binom{n}{2} crossings, attained by M^\star = \{(i,\, n+i) : 1 \le i \le n\}. For i < j \le n the arcs interleave, i < j < n+i < n+j, so all \binom{n}{2} arc-pairs cross; and no matching can exceed \binom{n}{2} because that is the total number of arc-pairs. (Confirmed by exhaustive enumeration for n \le 6: \max_\pi \mathrm{cr}(\pi) = \binom{n}{2}, achieved by M^\star.)

Step 2 — super-exponential lower bound. Each summand q_0^{\mathrm{cr}(\pi)} is positive, so retaining only the M^\star term,

  T_n(q_0) \;\ge\; q_0^{\binom{n}{2}}
  \;=\; \exp\!\Big( \tfrac{n(n-1)}{2}\,\ln q_0 \Big)
  \;=\; \exp\!\big(\Theta(n^2)\big),

since \ln q_0 > 0. The exponent is quadratic in n, so T_n(q_0) outgrows c^{\,n} for every constant c — super-exponential divergence. (The exact values T_n(q_0) = 3.11,\,16.7,\,131,\,1365,\,1.81\!\times\!10^4,\, 2.96\!\times\!10^5 for n=2,\dots,7 confirm a ratio T_n/T_{n-1} that grows with n rather than saturating, the signature of \exp(\Theta(n^2)).)

Step 3 — no q-Fock realisation. By Bożejko–Speicher, the q-deformed commutation relations a_i a_j^{\dagger} - q\, a_j^{\dagger} a_i = \delta_{ij} admit a positive (Fock-space) representation iff -1 \le q \le 1. At q_0 > 1 the associated Gram form fails to be positive semi-definite, so no q-Gaussian state on the q-Fock space exists.

Step 4 — a measure still exists. The moments T_n are those of the three-term recurrence x\,p_k = p_{k+1} + [k]_{q}\, p_{k-1} with [k]_q = 1 + q + \cdots + q^{k-1} (the Touchard–Riordan expansion of the q-Hermite moments). For q_0 > 1 every coefficient [k]_{q_0} is positive, so the Hankel determinants equal \prod_{k=1}^{n-1}[k]_{q_0}^{\,n-k} > 0 and, by Favard's theorem, probability measures with moments T_n(q_0) exist (for example \det H_3 = 1 + q_0 \approx 2.11 and \det H_4 \approx 14.88). By Step 2 none of them has a finite moment-generating function. The obstruction is therefore to the Fock-space construction, not to the existence of a measure. \square

sec:vertex-factorisation-feynman-preambl:
The factorisation of vertex operators across the exceptional divisor translates directly into the language of Feynman path integrals. Expanding the categorical propagator in the Schur–Weyl eigenbasis diagonalises the two-point amplitude across Wedderburn blocks, and the trace-collapse lemma shows that summing over intermediate polarization states reduces the Feynman loop trace to the Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M.

This section establishes the eigenbasis decomposition, proves the Feynman–Markov identification and categorical trace equivalence, and compiles the dictionary between perturbative quantum field theory and the categorical trace calculus. In the classical limit q \to 1, the q-deformed vertex weights collapse to the standard symmetric Dyson series.
lem:feynman-trace-collapse:
Lemma Path integral collapses to a finite sum on the eigenbasis. Suppose V_{\mathrm{phys}} = \varinjlim V^{\otimes n} admits the complete eigenbasis of (eigenbasis decomposition). Then the Feynman path integral

  \langle\psi_f|\psi_i\rangle
  =
  \int \mathcal{D}\phi\,e^{iS[\phi]/\hbar}

collapses to a finite weighted sum over the irreducible summands V_\lambda \otimes S_\lambda. No regularisation is needed because V^{\otimes n} has finitely many irreducible summands due to the semisimplicity of H_n(R, q) at non-root-of-unity q.
prf:feynman-trace-collapse:
Proof Proof that the path integral collapses on the eigenbasis. In Feynman's formulation, the transition amplitude between initial state |\psi_i\rangle and final state |\psi_f\rangle is

  \langle\psi_f|\psi_i\rangle
  =
  \int \mathcal{D}\phi\,e^{iS[\phi]/\hbar},

where the integral runs over all paths in configuration space. Now suppose that V_{\mathrm{phys}} = \varinjlim V^{\otimes n} admits the complete eigenbasis from (eigenbasis decomposition). Then every path \phi factors through a unique irreducible summand V_\lambda \otimes S_\lambda, and the continuum integral collapses to a finite weighted sum over irreducible summands.

No regularisation is needed: the sum has finitely many terms because V^{\otimes n} has finitely many irreducible summands (semisimplicity of H_n(R, q) at non-root-of-unity q). \square
lem:feynman-markov-identification:
Lemma Markov-weighted eigenbasis sum equals the Markov trace. Let q be real, not a root of unity, with q^2 + 1 \neq 0, and let \mathrm{tr}_M be a Markov trace on the Hecke tower at the parameter z = q^3/(q^2+1). For x \in H_n(R, q), the transition amplitude on the eigenbasis is the Markov-weighted sum of partial traces:

  \langle\psi_f|\psi_i\rangle_{\mathrm{eigenbasis}}
  :=
  \sum_{\lambda \vdash n}
  w_\lambda \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{S_\lambda}(x),

where w_\lambda is the Ocneanu weight of \lambda at z and \mathrm{tr}_{S_\lambda} is the trace of the seminormal representation S_\lambda. This amplitude equals \mathrm{tr}_M(x). The weight w_\lambda vanishes whenever \lambda has three or more rows, so only the partitions with \ell(\lambda) \leq 2 contribute, and for those

  w_\lambda = \frac{\dim_q(V_\lambda)}{\dim_q(V^{\otimes n})}
  = \frac{[\lambda_1 - \lambda_2 + 1]_q}{[2]_q^{\,n}}.
prf:feynman-markov-identification:
Proof Proof that the eigenbasis amplitude equals the Markov trace. Every Markov trace at z = q^3/(q^2+1) equals the Ocneanu-weighted sum of the seminormal block traces,

  \mathrm{tr}_M(x) = \sum_{\lambda \vdash n} w_\lambda \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{S_\lambda}(x),

for every n and every x \in H_n(R, q). This is the uniqueness of the Markov trace on the Hecke tower, established on the seminormal representations. The left side is the eigenbasis amplitude by definition, so the identity holds.

A partition with three or more rows contains the cell (2, 0), whose factor in the numerator of the Ocneanu weight vanishes at this z. Hence w_\lambda = 0 for \ell(\lambda) \geq 3, and the sum runs over \ell(\lambda) \leq 2 alone.

For the closed form, the Ocneanu weight at this z equals s_\lambda(1, q^2)/(1 + q^2)^n, where s_\lambda(1, q^2) is the Schur polynomial in two variables evaluated at (1, q^2). For \lambda = (\lambda_1, \lambda_2),

  s_\lambda(1, q^2)
  = q^{2\lambda_2}\,\frac{q^{2(\lambda_1 - \lambda_2 + 1)} - 1}{q^2 - 1}
  = q^{\lambda_1 + \lambda_2}\,[\lambda_1 - \lambda_2 + 1]_q,

and (1 + q^2)^n = q^n [2]_q^{\,n}. Since \lambda_1 + \lambda_2 = n, the powers of q cancel, and w_\lambda = [\lambda_1 - \lambda_2 + 1]_q / [2]_q^{\,n} = \dim_q(V_\lambda)/\dim_q(V^{\otimes n}). \square
prop:feynman-categorical-trace:
Proposition Feynman transition amplitude as categorical trace. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with \mathbf{C} = \mathbf{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)), V the fundamental representation, q real and not a root of unity, and \mathrm{tr}_M the Markov trace at z = q^3/(q^2+1). Let \varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A be a closed cycle with braid representative \beta \in B_n.

The Feynman transition amplitude evaluated on the knot-type eigenbasis equals the Jones--Markov trace of the braid representation in the Hecke algebra:

  \langle\psi_f|\psi_i\rangle_{\mathrm{eigenbasis}}
  =
  \sum_{\substack{\lambda \vdash n \\ \ell(\lambda) \leq 2}}
  w_\lambda \cdot \mathrm{tr}_{S_\lambda}\bigl(\rho_n(\beta)\bigr)
  =
  \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr),

where w_\lambda = \dim_q(V_\lambda)/\dim_q(V^{\otimes n}) = [\lambda_1 - \lambda_2 + 1]_q/[2]_q^{\,n}. The trace satisfies \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) and \mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n^{-1}) = (z - h)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) for x \in H_n(R, q), where h = q - q^{-1}.

The sum has \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 terms. The categorical mass at a single brane level is the absolute value of this amplitude:

  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)\big|_{\text{single level}}
  =
  \bigl|\mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr)\bigr|
  =
  \bigl|
  \langle\psi_f|\psi_i\rangle_{\mathrm{eigenbasis}}
  \bigr|.
prf:feynman-categorical-trace:
Proof Proof of Feynman transition amplitude as categorical trace. By (Markov identification), the Markov-weighted sum of seminormal block traces equals \mathrm{tr}_M\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr). Only partitions with at most two rows carry nonzero weight, and on those w_\lambda = \dim_q(V_\lambda)/\dim_q(V^{\otimes n}). The partitions of n with at most two rows are (n - k, k) for 0 \leq k \leq \lfloor n/2 \rfloor, so there are \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 terms.

The rule for \sigma_n^{-1} follows from the quadratic relation \sigma_n^{-1} = \sigma_n - h: \mathrm{tr}_M(x\sigma_n^{-1}) = \mathrm{tr}_M(x\sigma_n) - h\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x) = (z - h)\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x).

By (categorical mass as Markov trace), the categorical mass at a single brane level is |\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta))|, which by the first step is the absolute value of the eigenbasis amplitude. \square

prose:intro-kashiwara-jones-quantum-dilo:
Two fundamental structures of quantum topology meet on the Hecke algebra H_n(q): Kashiwara's crystal basis at q \to 0, which governs the combinatorial branching of irreducible modules, and the Jones polynomial at finite q, which governs link invariants. The bridge between them is the quantum dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) (and its compact Faddeev counterpart \Phi_q).

This section establishes the Kashiwara–Jones alternation identity, defines the canonical braid interface composition, and proves structural gap invariance in rigid monoidal categories. Stratifying the quantum dilogarithm by cellular depth in the (q, z) bi-completion shows that finite-level truncations of the Pochhammer product converge in the z-Habiro topology, while the archimedean image of the five-term quantum dilogarithm relation recovers the Rogers pentagon identity on the Bloch group B(\mathbb{C}) and the Pachner 2–3 move on the Borromean complement.

The categorical precision ladder exhibits an empirical alternating pattern in its coefficients:

2 Kashiwara \tilde f_1^\dagger \tilde f_1 return amplitude b^2
3 Classical-limit Jones J_{\text{Hopf}}(q=1) = -2

This alternation stems from the fact that the Kashiwara and Jones contributions arise from different moduli spaces. The Kashiwara crystal lives in the moduli of finite-dimensional U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2) representations. The Jones polynomial lives in the moduli of knot complements. The Markov trace sits at the intersection, computing the closure of a typed braid that lives in H_n(q) and produces a link invariant.

The parity rule governs this alternation. Even k stays within the Kashiwara block, as the Hecke quadratic reduces \sigma_i^k to a polynomial within H_n(q), generating no link invariant. Odd k produces an even crossing number upon closure, yielding a topological link invariant. The Jones value of this link emerges via the Markov trace.

The precision ladder utilizes a Gröbner-Buchberger filtration indexed by jet order. The Hecke quadratic increases jet order by one. The precision-ladder rungs correspond exactly to distinct jet orders, with the twist scaling as \hbar_q^{2k}. Hyperbolic closures contribute topological volume and integer Jones values, while torus operators remain geometrically trivial. The alternating pattern breaks down at c_5, c_6 because mixed-order links and cross-block Hoefsmit couplings introduce simultaneous Kashiwara and Jones contributions.

prop:rigid-monoidal-structural-gap-invar:
Proposition Convention-independence of the structural gap: the brane-tower factors through the rigid monoidal Markov trace on the Type-B-folded Hecke category. Let \mathbf{C} = \mathbf{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) be the rigid monoidal category. Let \tau \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^{\otimes n}) \to \mathbb{C}_q be the canonical Markov trace. Define the categorical structural gap for a confined particle \mathfrak{H} as:

  \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H}) := B_{\mathrm{AME}}(\mathfrak{H}) - m_e \cdot \rho \cdot \bigl|\tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})\bigr|.

The value \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H}) depends only on the categorical-trace invariant \tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}). It is strictly invariant under any choice of operator-volume convention.

The Markov trace \tau is uniquely determined by the categorical axioms up to the choice of parameter z. Operator-volume conventions vary only the non-categorical regularizer. Differences in regularizer choices cancel into the identical \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}} value.

The Markov trace is not invariant under the spin involution \sigma_i \mapsto \sigma_i^{-1}. At z = q^3/(q^2+1), \tau(\sigma_i) = q^3/(q^2+1) while \tau(\sigma_i^{-1}) = 1/\bigl(q(q^2+1)\bigr). That involution respects the Hecke relation only together with q \mapsto q^{-1}, and \tau is equivariant for that combined bar involution, \tau(\bar x) = \overline{\tau(x)}. So spin invariance of the LP-dual selections does not follow from properties of \tau.

Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the algebraic→archimedean wall. It applies q-deformation identities over an abstract coefficient ring and specializes them to real-valued observables at q_0.
prf:rigid-monoidal-structural-gap-invari:
Proof Proof of prop rigid monoidal structural gap invariance. Recall the definition from the statement block: for a confined particle \mathfrak{H},

  \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H})
  \;=\;
  B_{\mathrm{AME}}(\mathfrak{H})
  \;-\;
  m_e \cdot \rho \cdot \bigl|\tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})\bigr|,

where B_{\mathrm{AME}} is the tabulated experimental binding, m_e and \rho are fixed calibration constants, and \tau \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A^{\otimes n}) \to \mathbb{C}_q is the canonical Markov trace. An operator-volume convention is a rule for evaluating the divergent brane tower \sum_i \Phi_q(z_i) attached to \mathfrak{H}; it prescribes (i) which tower summands enter and with what weights or depths, and (ii) which operator data feed the tower argument. The only quantity in the definition of \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}} that could conceivably depend on such a rule is \tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}). The proof factors into three steps.

Step 1: uniqueness of the Markov trace. For H_n(q) at generic q, the functional satisfying M1 (cyclicity), M2 (the Markov axiom \mathrm{tr}^{(n)}(x \cdot \sigma_{n-1}) = z \cdot \mathrm{tr}^{(n-1)}(x) with the framework parameter z = q^{3}/(q^{2}+1)), and M3 (\mathrm{tr}(1) = 1) is unique (Markov-trace uniqueness; Jones [jones1987], Wenzl [wenzl1988]). Consequently any two evaluation routes that compute a functional obeying M1–M3 — seminormal-form evaluation, recursive Markov peeling, or the Wenzl bridge — return the same value \tau(\beta) on any given braid \beta, and in particular the same magnitude |\tau(\beta)|.

Step 2: every probed convention factors through the same categorical trace. Each of the six brane-tower convention families probed in Brane tower lives in the z-Habiro ring §"Surviving claims after closure attempts" is, by its defining prescription, a regularization of the divergent analytic \Phi_q tower. Case by case:

  1. Scalar uniform-k truncates the tower at a fixed depth k; it acts only on the tower index set.
  2. \ell n_0 + k is a level-selection variant of the same truncation; again only the tower index set changes.
  3. Per-eigenvalue operator-valued replaces the scalar tower argument with the eigenvalue-resolved operator argument; the trace functional applied to the categorical factor still satisfies M1–M3.
  4. Multiplicity / Type-B-fold reweights tower summands by folded-crystal multiplicities; the fold acts on the index set of the tower, not on the trace functional.
  5. Pair-knot product-volume substitutes pair-knot composite volumes for per-generator volumes inside the tower argument.
  6. Pair-knot Markov-trace evaluates the pair-knot composite by a trace functional satisfying M1–M3, which by Step 1 coincides with the canonical trace on the composite element.

In every case the convention's output factors as a convention-dependent tower regularizer composed with one and the same categorical evaluation: none of the six prescriptions modifies the functional applied to \beta_{\mathfrak{H}}, which in each family obeys M1–M3 and therefore, by Step 1, equals the canonical Markov trace. The conventions differ only in how the divergent tower — a quantity that does not appear in the definition of \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}} — is regularized.

Step 3: convention-independence of \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}. Let c and c' be any two probed conventions. By Steps 1 and 2, the categorical factor computed under either convention is the canonical value, so |\tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})|_c = |\tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})|_{c'}. The remaining ingredients B_{\mathrm{AME}}(\mathfrak{H}), m_e, and \rho make no reference to the convention. Substituting into the defining formula,

  \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H})\big|_{c}
  \;=\;
  \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H})\big|_{c'},

so \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(\mathfrak{H}) depends only on the categorical-trace invariant \tau(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}) and is strictly invariant under the choice of operator-volume convention. \square

Falsifiable predictions

  1. Convention-independence of \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}({}^3\mathrm{He}). Compute |\tau(\beta_{{}^3\mathrm{He}})| via Hoefsmit seminormal (per-eigenvalue), via the recursive symbolic Markov peel, and via the Wenzl bridge at 50 dps. All three should give the same |\tau| to 50 dps; the resulting \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}} should be atom-dependent but convention-independent.

  2. Convention-dependent regularizer dominates the brane-tower variation. The non-categorical brane-tower regularization contributions vary by orders of magnitude across the six canonical evaluation families — but their difference from |\tau| is the same non-categorical regularizer. The structural gap \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}} should be the same across all probed conventions, on each atom separately.

  3. Magic-shell decomposition. \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(Z, N) should decompose as \Delta_{\mathrm{cat}}(Z, N) = \Delta_0(A) + \mathbb{1}_{Z \in \mathrm{magic}} \cdot \Delta_p + \mathbb{1}_{N \in \mathrm{magic}} \cdot \Delta_n with \Delta_p = \Delta_n (the Z\leftrightarrowN symmetry constraint). This is the precise content of the magic-shell stabilization conjecture.
prop:cell-depth-truncation:
Proposition Cell-depth truncation of a trace: the depth-k parts vanish above k_\star(x), any weighted sum stabilises there, and the truncated \Phi_q product never stabilises. Let A=H_n(K,q) be split semisimple over a field K, with central primitive idempotents e_\lambda, irreducible characters \chi_\lambda and GB-depth a(\lambda) as in Cell-depth filtration of Z(H_n(q)). For a trace \tau on A and x\in A put

E_k:=\sum_{a(\lambda)=k}e_\lambda,\qquad \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x):=\tau(E_kx),\qquad k_\star(x):=\max\{a(\lambda):\chi_\lambda(x)\ne0\}

(k_\star(x):=0 if no \chi_\lambda(x) is nonzero). Then for every trace \tau, every x\in A and all weights (\alpha_k)\subset K:

  1. \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x)=0 for all k>k_\star(x);
  2. \sum_{k=0}^{K'}\alpha_k\mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{k_\star(x)}\alpha_k\mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x) for every K'\ge k_\star(x);
  3. \sum_{k=0}^{k_\star(x)}\mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x)=\tau(x).
  4. (Vacuous on braids.) If x=T_w for some w\in S_n, or x is the image of a braid, then k_\star(x)=\binom n2, the largest value of a. So the truncation in items 1–3 removes nothing on these inputs. (This item invokes the Kazhdan–Lusztig two-sided cell properties cited in the proof.)
  5. (The truncated \Phi_q product does not stabilise.) Let F be a field, q,z\in F^\times with 1-q^{-j}z\ne0 for all j\ge1, and \Phi_q^{[\le K']}(z):=\prod_{j=1}^{K'}(1-q^{-j}z)^{-1}. Then \Phi_q^{[\le K'+1]}(z)\ne\Phi_q^{[\le K']}(z) for every K'. Hence no sequence S_{K'} can satisfy both S_{K'}=\Phi_q^{[\le K']}(z) for all K' and S_{K'}=S_{k_0} for all K'\ge k_0.

Items 1–3 hold for any function on partitions in place of a; the content of the statement is the choice of a, which comes from the Kazhdan–Lusztig two-sided ideals of A and not from any mass datum. Setting the level-k term equal to \Phi_q^{[\le k]}(z_i)-\Phi_q^{[\le k-1]}(z_i) defines a different object from \tau(E_kx), and the two must not share the symbol \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}.
prf:cell-depth-truncation:
Proof Proof of the cell-depth truncation statements. Items 1–3. Every trace on the split semisimple A is \tau=\sum_\mu y_\mu\chi_\mu, and \chi_\mu(e_\lambda x)=\delta_{\lambda\mu}\chi_\lambda(x), so \tau(e_\lambda x)=y_\lambda\chi_\lambda(x). If k>k_\star(x), every \lambda with a(\lambda)=k has \chi_\lambda(x)=0, so \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x)=\sum_{a(\lambda)=k}y_\lambda\chi_\lambda(x)=0. Item 2 follows because the terms with k_\star<k\le K' vanish. For item 3, \sum_kE_k=\sum_\lambda e_\lambda=1, so \sum_k\mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_\tau(x)=\tau(x), and the terms above k_\star are 0.

Item 4. The index character T_s\mapsto q gives \chi_{(n)}(T_w)=q^{\ell(w)} and, on a braid image, q to the exponent sum. Both are units, so (n) lies in the support. And a(\lambda)=\sum_i\binom{\lambda_i}2\le\binom n2 with equality only at \lambda=(n).

Item 5. Put P=\Phi_q^{[\le K']}(z)\ne0 and u=1-q^{-(K'+1)}z. Then \Phi_q^{[\le K'+1]}(z)=Pu^{-1}, and Pu^{-1}=P would force u=1, so q^{-(K'+1)}z=0, contradicting q,z\ne0. For the consequence apply this at K'=k_0. The hypotheses are satisfiable, for example q=2, z=1 over \mathbb Q.

Scope. Items 1–4 hold for an arbitrary depth function on a finite index set. The Kazhdan–Lusztig basis and the cell–irreducible correspondence are cited [Kazhdan–Lusztig 1979] rather than proved here, and were checked exactly for n\le5. \blacksquare
conj:phi-q-categorical-truncation:

  \mathfrak{m}^{\mathrm{tower}}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(T_w) = \sum_{k=0}^{k_\star(T_w)} \alpha_k \cdot \mathfrak{m}^{(k)}_{q,\mathcal{K}}(T_w) = \sum_i \Phi_q^{[\leq k_\star(T_w)]}(z_i).

The depth k_\star(T_w) is exactly the maximum GB-depth among the support partitions. Truncation at any deeper level k \geq k_\star yields the identical categorical value.

Scope. With GB-depth defined as Lusztig's a-function (Cell-depth filtration of Z(H_n(q))); the three earlier readings (ideal power, Coxeter length, rewrite depth) are each degenerate or not compatible with the blocks. With that choice the statement splits in two:

  • The second equality, which identifies the level-K partial sum with \sum_i\Phi_q^{[\le K]}(z_i) at every level, is false together with stabilisation: \Phi_q^{[\le K+1]}(z)\ne\Phi_q^{[\le K]}(z) for every z\ne0 (item 5 of the same proposition). At a single level that equality is a definition of a residual, not a theorem.

def:q-pochhammer-partial-product:
Definition q-Pochhammer partial product \Phi_n(x; q). The q-Pochhammer partial product at depth n is the finite rational function:

  \Phi_n(x; q) := \prod_{k=0}^{n-1} \frac{1}{1 - x q^k} = \frac{1}{(x; q)_n}.
rem:q-pochhammer-partial-product-remark:
Remark Poles, recurrence and truncation of the q-Pochhammer partial product. The denominator (x; q)_n carries simple roots at x = q^{-k}. This finite product is structurally valid at the q_0 > 1 aether. It corresponds exactly to the categorical truncation \Phi_q^{[\leq n]}.

The partial product satisfies the one-step recurrence \Phi_{n+1} = \Phi_n / (1 - x q^n), which mirrors the filtration induction step. The denominator zeros x = q^{-k} define the cuspidal boundary of the JSJ geometry. The algebraic engine uses these zeros as exact initial seeds for the Newton-Raphson solver.
def:quantum-bloch-group:
Definition Quantum Bloch group and the pentagon identity. The classical Bloch group \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) is defined by the five-term relation of the dilogarithm \mathrm{Li}_2. The quantum Bloch group \mathfrak{B}(q)(R) replaces this with the pentagon identity of the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q:

  \Phi_q(u)\,\Phi_q(v)
  \;=\;
  \Phi_q(v)\,\Phi_q(uv)\,\Phi_q(u)
  \qquad \text{where } uv = qvu

In the form e_q(a)\,e_q(b) = e_q(b)\,e_q(-ba)\,e_q(a) with ab = qba, this is the Faddeev–Kashaev pentagon relation, a quantum analogue of the Rogers five-term relation [kirillov1995, §2.5, Thm. I and Cor. 11]. This identity is the Yang–Baxter equation in exponential form.

The connection to the QOU framework — why \Phi_1 is a quantum dilogarithm, the Kashaev invariant, and the pre-archimedean refinement of \mathfrak{B}(q) over the Habiro ring — is developed in the follow-on remark. A functorial setting for state-sum invariants built from quantum dilogarithms is quantum hyperbolic field theory: for each odd N it assigns to a 3-manifold with a framed tangle and a PSL(2,\mathbb{C})-character a tensor built from matrix dilogarithms [baseilhac-benedetti2007, §1, §2.1].

Branch ambiguity and the extended Bloch group (literature). The ordinary Bloch group \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) carries the single-valued Bloch–Wigner function, which recovers only the volume. The multivaluedness of \mathrm{Li}_2 is removed by passing to the extended Bloch group \widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}) of Goette and Zickert, as surveyed in [arxiv-2304.12545v1, §3]: generators are pairs [u,v] with e^u + e^v = 1, the relations are a lifted version of the five-term relation, and the regulator \sum_j [u_j,v_j] \mapsto \sum_j \bigl(L(v_j) + \tfrac12 u_j v_j - \tfrac{\pi^2}{6}\bigr), with L(v) = \mathrm{Li}_2(1-e^v), is well defined modulo 4\pi^2 on that relation. It is the extended group, not the ordinary one, on which a complex-valued dilogarithm invariant is single-valued. The survey is a secondary source: the lifted five-term relation is stated there without proof, and the primary papers of Goette and Zickert are not in the bibliography. Neumann's original construction is registered [neumann2004, §1]. The volume computations in this chapter use only the single-valued Bloch–Wigner function D on the ordinary Bloch group rather than the lifted five-term relation on \widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}).
rem:quantum-bloch-group-framework-connec:
Remark Quantum Bloch group: framework connection and the pre-archimedean refinement. The pentagon identity of the quantum dilogarithm \Phi_q — the Yang–Baxter equation in exponential form — connects to the QOU framework as follows:

  1. The braid group B_n is generated by the Yang–Baxter equation \sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}.

  2. The Hecke relation \sigma_i^2 = h_{\mathrm{A}}\sigma_i + 1 is the linearisation of the quantum pentagon identity.

  3. The traced volumes \hat{V}_i(q) satisfy the Hecke relation because they are matrix elements of \rho(\sigma_i) in the standard representation.

  4. The algebraic quantum volume \mathrm{Vol}_q = \prod \hat{V}_i therefore satisfies the pentagon identity (multiplicatively), and its logarithm \Phi_1 = \tfrac{1}{2}\sum \ln(\hat{V}_i \cdot \overline{\hat{V}_i}) satisfies the five-term relation (additively).

This explains why \Phi_1 is a quantum dilogarithm: the traced volumes are exponentials of quantum dilogarithm values, and their product lives in the quantum Bloch group. The regulator map \mathfrak{B}(q) \to \mathbb{R} sends the algebraic volume to the hyperbolic volume, recovering \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) from the algebraic data. The classical counterpart of this sentence is proved for the A-polynomial curve Y of a knot rather than for \mathfrak{B}(q): the regulator 1-form \eta(l,m) = \log|l|\,d\arg m - \log|m|\,d\arg l is exact on the hyperbolic component, and its loop integrals, divided by 4\pi^2, lie in \tfrac{1}{N}\mathbb{Z}, where N is the order of the symbol \{l,m\} in K_2(\mathbb{C}(Y)) [li-wang2006, Thm. 3.3]. That theorem does not treat the quantum Bloch group, so the passage from \mathfrak{B}(q) to the regulator above is not covered by it.

Two published constructions sit beside this picture, each with a limit. On the classical side, the branch ambiguity of the dilogarithm is resolved by the extended Bloch group \widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}) of flattened shape parameters: the extended Rogers dilogarithm gives a well-defined map R\colon\widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C})\to\mathbb{C}/\pi^2\mathbb{Z}, and its composite with H_3(\mathrm{PSL}(2,\mathbb{C});\mathbb{Z})\to\widehat{\mathcal{B}}(\mathbb{C}) computes volume and Chern--Simons invariant together, where the ordinary Bloch group fixes the Chern--Simons part only up to an additive ambiguity [neumann2004, §1]. On the q-side, for a number field F Garoufalidis, Scholze, Wheeler and Zagier construct a Habiro ring of F and a regulator K_3(F)\to\mathrm{Pic} of that ring, whose image line bundles carry q-series from perturbative Chern--Simons theory as sections; this geometry disappears after (q-1)-completion [wagner2025, §1.1]. Neither construction is the quantum Bloch group \mathfrak{B}(q) of this paper: the first is classical, and the second lives over the Habiro ring of a number field rather than over \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} with the bar involution. They are recorded as the nearest literature statements of the same shape, not as cases of the claim above.

The Kashaev invariant is the state sum version: \langle K \rangle = \sum_j \prod_{\text{tetrahedra}} \Phi_q(x_j)^{\pm 1}, living in the Habiro ring. For the Borromean rings, this gives \langle \mathcal{B}_3 \rangle whose archimedean evaluation yields 8G.

Pre-archimedean side: \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]})

The quantum Bloch group \mathfrak{B}(q) has a natural pre-archimedean refinement over the Habiro ring \widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]} (Habiro 2002), without passing through the complex numbers:

Pre-archimedean \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}) \tfrac{1}{2}\sum \ln(\hat{V}_i \cdot \overline{\hat{V}_i}) Habiro ring; bar = q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}
Archimedean (\tau_{\mathrm{arch}} at real q_0, real \hat{V}_i) \mathcal{B}(\mathbb{C}) \sum \ln\lvert\hat{V}_i\rvert Borel regulator r_1: K_1(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R}

The bar-involution form \tfrac{1}{2}\ln(V \cdot \overline{V}) at the pre-archimedean level is what the framework uses for \rho_K's single-generator piece ([prop:rho-k-graded-expansion](rho-k-graded-expansion.md)). At the archimedean specialization with real q_0 and real \hat{V}_i, this reduces to the classical Borel regulator \sum \ln\lvert\hat{V}_i\rvert — the form that appears in Borromean rings represent a non-trivial element of K_3(\mathbb{C}) / Bloch group with regulator r_2 = 8G under the Beilinson regulator r_2: K_3(\mathbb{C}) \to \mathbb{R}.

This makes the QOU framework's K-theoretic content categorically explicit: \rho_K is a graded regulator on \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}) whose archimedean evaluation at q_0 \in \mathbb{R}_{>1} recovers the classical hyperbolic K_3 regulator. The pre-archimedean form respects the Hecke bar-involution; the archimedean form respects the standard \mathbb{R}-valued K-theory.

This refines the discussion in Borromean rings represent a non-trivial element of K_3(\mathbb{C}) / Bloch group with regulator r_2 = 8G: the framework's working object is the pre-archimedean \mathfrak{B}(\widehat{\mathbb{Z}[q]}), and the Beilinson regulator r_2 is the archimedean realization of the graded \rho_K.
prop:q-rogers-pentagon-archimedean:
Proposition Post-τ pentagon = pre-τ pentagon + q-log² Rogers correction. The pre-\tau bare pentagon operates formally in the Hopf algebra without log-squared terms. Under the archimedean realization functor, the post-\tau pentagon acquires the \log_q^2 correction:

  \mathrm{Li}_2^q(u) + \mathrm{Li}_2^q(v) - \mathrm{Li}_2^q(uv) - \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\alpha) - \mathrm{Li}_2^q(\beta) = \log_q\!\!\left(\frac{1-u}{1-uv}\right) \cdot \log_q\!\!\left(\frac{1-v}{1-uv}\right) + O\bigl((q-1)^2\bigr).

The realization functor introduces rational denominators, triggering the \log_q^2 Rogers correction. This correction anchors the post-\tau pentagon as the definitive identity for the analytic Volume-conjecture framework. The O((q-1)^2) residual acts as the formal testable prediction for archimedean convergence.
prf:q-rogers-pentagon-archimedean:
Proof Proof of q rogers pentagon archimedean. (Classical limit and q-deformation.)

Classical limit (q = 1). Set q = 1. The q-integers reduce to ordinary integers, [n]_q \to n, and \mathrm{Li}_2^q(z) \to \mathrm{Li}_2(z) = \sum z^n / n^2. The identity (R) reduces to the classical Rogers–Abel five-term identity [Rogers, 1907; Abel, 1826]:

  \mathrm{Li}_2(u) + \mathrm{Li}_2(v) - \mathrm{Li}_2(uv) -
  \mathrm{Li}_2(\alpha) - \mathrm{Li}_2(\beta) =
  \log\!\!\left(\frac{1-u}{1-uv}\right) \cdot \log\!\!\left(\frac{1-v}{1-uv}\right).

This is a classical, fully-proven result (Lewin, Polylogarithms and Associated Functions 1981, §1.6). It is the archimedean shadow of the bare pentagon (P): when q = 1, the pre-\tau identity acquires the explicit \log^2 correction.

q-deformation extension. For generic q, the q-log correction \log_q(x) = \sum_n (-1)^{n+1}(x-1)^n / [n]_q generalises the classical \log. The proposed identity (R) is the natural q-deformation: \log \to \log_q.
